subject: Harmonized commit swap + annualization path for Orbit Health renewal
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@orbithealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Harmonized commit swap + annualization path for Orbit Health renewal

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, I put together three practical options to align your mid-contract growth (the 250k token uplift from Q3) with your upcoming renewal so you don't get double-billed across two cycles. The goal is to keep unit economics predictable for Orbit while letting you scale now. High-level options attached in the spreadsheet; summary below.

Option A — Immediate top-up (simplest):
- Orbit purchases an immediate 250k token top-up at a discounted uplift rate (10% off list).
- Top-up runs until next renewal; commit stays the same at contract anniversary.
- Pro: fastest to implement, minimal paperwork.
- Con: two separate invoices this year.

Option B — Harmonized commit swap + annualization (preferred for predictability):
- We move 250k tokens into your main commit and annualize across remaining contract months (pro-rata), offering blended pricing that yields approx 12% effective discount vs. ad-hoc top-ups.
- We co-term any add-on usage to the renewal date; single invoice at renewal.
- Pro: single renewal cadence and smoother unit economics.
- Con: requires a short amendment and PO update.

Option C — Phased amortized purchase w/ pay-over-time:
- Purchase the 250k uplift now but amortize the cost over the remaining term in 3 installments; apply a 6% service credit if paid upfront.
- Pro: cash smoothing for Orbit.
- Con: bookkeeping complexity.

Requested ask from Orbit: which option do you prefer and whether procurement would like us to prepare an amendment (Option B recommended by our team).

I attached a spreadsheet (pricing_scenarios.xlsx) with line-item math and a draft amendment (signature-ready-amendment.docx) you can circulate to your procurement team.

Next steps: if Option B works, we can issue an amendment + updated SOW and route for signature within 48 hours.

Thanks, and happy to hop on a 20-min call if you want to walk the numbers.

—
Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0142
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@orbithealth.com>

Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Harmonized commit swap + annualization path for Orbit Health renewal

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear options. A few immediate items from procurement and finance:
1) For Option B, can you show the net MRR impact on our current billing (we'd like to avoid a big spike in the renewal invoice).
2) Does the blended pricing assume we keep the same model variant? We are evaluating a lower-cost quantized variant for internal dev traffic.
3) Any SLA implications if we shift tokens into the committed pool (we have some regulated workloads running on Dedicated).

Procurement asked for a one-pager summary they can circulate. Can you produce that and include the exact amendment language for our PO folks?

If Option B materially smooths cost and protects performance, procurement said they'd prioritize the amendment.

Thanks — cc'd procurement (Samir) for visibility.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
VP of Product — Orbit Health
elena.ruiz@orbithealth.com

[Attachment: Orbit_renewal_questions.pdf (procurement questions)]
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@orbithealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Orbit Health Procurement <procurement@orbithealth.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Harmonized commit swap + annualization path for Orbit Health renewal

Elena / Samir —

Thanks for the points. Quick responses inline:  
1) Net MRR / Billing impact (Option B):
- The blended rate spreads the incremental cost across remaining 8 months => ~31% uplift on monthly invoice for remaining term but leads to a single, smaller renewal delta vs paying top-ups + renewal. See tab "MRR view" in pricing_scenarios.xlsx.

2) Model variant:
- The blended pricing example assumes a like-for-like model. If you shift dev traffic to the quantized variant, we can carve out a dev bucket (separate metering) and apply a 20% lower per-token rate there; committed tokens stay tied to the nominated serving model. We will document variant mapping in the amendment.

3) SLA:
- No change to SLA for Dedicated workloads — topology/priority for committed pools will be preserved. We include a clause in the amendment to keep the same capacity reservation and latency SLOs.

I attached the one-pager summary and updated draft amendment language (SOW_v1.3.pdf + signature-ready-amendment.docx). If procurement approves the language, Ben and I will route a DocuSign.

Proposed cadence:
- Wed 6/23: Procurement confirms preferred option + minor redlines.
- Thu 6/24 AM: We send amendment in DocuSign.
- Thu 6/24 EOD: Try to secure PO update so billing can reflect annualization in July invoice.

If you want, I can do 15 minutes tomorrow to walk procurement through the MRR tab.

—
Jordan
